data.title: Why Qualys stock is trading up today
data.description:
What happened?

Shares of cybersecurity cloud platform provider Qualys jumped 6.6% in the morning session after a rebound in technology stocks lifted major U.S. equity indexes during a holiday-shortened trading session.

CNBC reported that the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged higher by 1.18% to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 edged higher by 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.31% to 24,129.50. According to the report, U.S. exchanges closed early following the Thanksgiving holiday, while the Dow and S&P 500 finished the week up more than 5% and the Nasdaq gained more than 6%.

Technology stocks led the advance, as Meta Platforms rose more than 3%, Amazon rose about 4%, Broadcom rose almost 4% and Anthropic soared nearly 11%, the report said. The rebound followed earlier market weakness tied to investor concerns over artificial intelligence debt financing, signs of moderation in capital expenditures and expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases, according to the report.

Broader rallies in technology stocks can lift investor sentiment toward software companies across the market. When buyers return to growth-oriented sectors after a pullback, share prices of individual technology businesses often move higher together.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down and closed the day at $206.60, up 5.2% from the previous close.

What is the market telling us

Qualys’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock gained 5.5% on the news that CrowdStrike announced a definitive all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to acquire Zscaler, uniting endpoint protection and zero-trust network security.

The mega-deal marks one of the largest consolidation moves in software history, directly influencing cybersecurity valuations across public markets. By integrating Zscaler into its Falcon platform, CrowdStrike aims to offer an all-in-one security architecture that protects both devices and cloud network traffic. Zero-trust security operates on the principle of never trusting and always verifying any user or device attempting to access private networks.

For investors, this massive transaction underscores escalating enterprise demand for comprehensive cybersecurity suites rather than fragmented point solutions, driving heightened interest and trading activity in both companies.

Qualys is up 68.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $220.23 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $230.29 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Qualys’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,639.

data.title: Robusta coffee heads away from 3-year low; raw sugar gains 10% weekly
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE headed further away from this week's 3-year lows on Friday amid lacklustre farmer selling in top grower Vietnam, while raw sugar posted a 10.2% price gain this week, recovering from a three-month low last week.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled up $91, or 3.2%, at $2,923 a metric ton, after setting a 3-year low of $2,709 on Wednesday.

* "Farmers are increasingly reluctant to sell," said a dealer based in Vietnam.

* He explained that if prices don't recover, he expects farmers to sell at most 35% of their crop before the Tet holiday in February, as they are banking on this year's dry weather and next year's El Nino peak to tighten supplies.

* Arabica coffee rose 2.1% to $2.7555 per lb, after hitting a five-month low on Wednesday.

* Dealers noted a sharp recovery in the Brazilian currency following the appointment of a new finance minister. The real gained 9% this week.

* "A stronger real gives Brazilian producers fewer reais per dollar sold. That tends to slow farmer selling and support flat price," said Tomas Araujo, a broker with StoneX.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar (SBH7) settled up 0.43 cent, or 2.3%, at 18.77 cents per lb, having hit a fresh one-month high of 19.10 cents earlier. The market gained 10.2% this week.

* France's main sugar groups Tereos and Cristal Union have offered financial support to beet growers hit by drought and heatwaves, seeking to maintain plantings for the 2027 crop as Europe faces a sugar shortfall.

* The gains in the Brazilian currency also offered support to the sugar market, dealers said.

* The global sugar deficit in the 2026/27 season will be slightly larger than previously expected, with a weaker outlook for production in India, Green Pool forecast.

* Itau BBA has cut its forecast for sugarcane crushing in Brazil's key center-south region in 2026/27 to between 620 million and 640 million metric tons, down from 645 million tons.

* White sugar rose 0.6% to $525.40 a ton, having hit a fresh one-month high of $534.40 earlier.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​settled up £71, or 1.7%, to £4,291 per ton, having hit its highest since late October at £4,335.

* The supply outlook continues to worsen in top growers Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador, though there is ample availability of cocoa for now from the bumper 2025/26 crop.

* New York cocoa rose 1.2% to $5,499 a ton.

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Stronger Friday
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were stronger on Friday, benefiting from spillover in sharp increases in Chicago soybeans and soyoil.

Additional spillover came from gains in Chicago soymeal, Malaysian palm oil and European rapeseed. Losses in crude oil limited the upside in canola and other veg oils.

The January canola contract remained slightly above its 20- and 200-day moving averages but remained well short of its other technical levels.

The Canadian Grain Commission reported for the week ended Nov. 22 that year-to-date canola exports climbed to 2.86 million tonnes this marketing year, compared to 1.93 million the same time last year. Cumulative domestic use of canola hit 4.01 million tonnes versus 3.69 million a year ago.

The Canadian dollar dipped lower on Friday afternoon, with the loonie at 70.17 U.S. cents, compared to Thursday's close of 70.21.

There were 69,512 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to 24,722 on Thursday. Spreading accounted for 44,428 contracts traded.

data.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Fall on Milder Near-Term Weather Outlook — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. natural gas futures settle lower with the Nymex January contract falling 4.5% to $3.491/mmBtu in its first trading day at the front of the curve. "The overnight forecasts took some heating demand out of December 2-6, giving traders less reason to pay up for gas heading into the first week of the month," Gelber & Associates says in a note. Further out in the forecast, both U.S. and European models added cold for Dec. 7-10, the firm says. data.title: Silver Price Analysis: XAG/USD Faces Deeper Losses as $40 Support Nears
data.description:
The week's fall in silver prices highlights the fragility of the market. This week's slide in silver prices is a sign of the market's fragility.

Silver’s Weekly Decline Exposes a Weakening Market

Silver has continued its downward trend, falling 15.37% over the past week to around $41.23 per ounce, as seen on the Trading Economics chart.

The Investing.com daily chart also shows silver lost 3.86% during the session, ending around $41.20 after the lowest price it hit during today's session was $40.77.

The higher-level chart pattern indicates a long-term return from the August highs around $70. Source: TradingEconomics

Since then, successive lower highs and lower lows have been observed, suggesting that sellers have been in control. The drop was picked up after the metal's recovery in November collapsed, taking the price back towards the $53 mark.

The price is in line with the overall decline of precious metals. The drop in gold and silver prices was blamed in a November 21 Wall Street Journal report on rising interest rates for U.S. government bonds and a stronger U.S. dollar and on additional rate increases by the Federal Reserve. Silver's industrial ties make it a weak performer when investors are nervous about economic growth, too.

Technical Outlook: $40 Becomes the Next Major Test

The daily chart shows a bearish pattern with the price of silver moving into the lower part of the range shown and near the bottom of the daily consolidation range. The first significant support reference is the latest session's low at $40.77. The next psychological level that traders should pay attention to is $40 below.

However, if silver continues to close below $40 every day, it could bring additional downside pressure to silver and further confirm the ongoing series of lower lows. But if there is a temporary drop below support with a fast bounce up, it might mean that the buyers are trying to cover the selling pressure.

According to the chart, the positive side is that 42.80–43.60 seems to be a point of initial resistance as per the opening and higher levels of the recent daily trading session. Source: investing.com

If the price can resume its recovery from this area, it may resume its move toward $45, where there was some selling pressure previously. A wider range of resistance is seen in the $47-48 zone, a previous consolidation area before the prior breakdown.

All other technical evidence is negative. In its technical summary for November, Investing.com said silver is a "strong sell" as the RSI was below the neutral 50 level and the majority of moving averages indicated selling pressure.

What Traders Should Watch Next?

The first question that needs to be asked is if silver can sustain the $40 support level during a resumption of trading. If prices fall below it, then the bearish argument would be reinforced, and if they rise above it, perhaps for the first time, it would suggest that selling pressure is easing.

US dollar, Treasury yields, and Federal Reserve communications should also be watched by traders. Any further improvement in yields and a stronger dollar will remain a headwind for non-yielding precious metals. However, if the economy releases weaker data or the policy stance is less hawkish, there will be a chance to recover.

Industrial-demand expectations are also an element to consider, as silver is used in the manufacturing sector as well as the monetary market. Even if gold stabilizes, the prospects for buying will be constrained by signs of weaker industrial activity.

The technical picture is currently tilted towards sellers. For traders to assert that the recent pullback is over, they must get some of that nearby resistance cleared before the big move to the downside resumes. Until then, the $40 level is the key price to look at for a possible stabilization versus another leg lower.

data.title: CBOT soybeans rally, supported by stronger Brazilian real, export demand
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures rallied to a one-month high on Friday on support from a stronger Brazilian real, higher soymeal prices and steady export demand for US soybeans.

  • Brazilian assets rallied after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva tapped a market-friendly bank executive to be his next finance ‌chief, following weeks of investor concern over the fiscal direction of the leftist leader's upcoming fourth term.

  • Export demand for soybeans has also been steady.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net weekly export sales of 755,800 metric tons of soybeans. The agency also reported sales of 132,000 tons of soybeans to the Netherlands for 2026/27 delivery.

  • Investors are weighing whether exports to China will be affected, as the top soy importer was already on pace to meet its annual purchasing commitment, while a disappointing harvest in South America could shift demand toward US soybeans.

  • The soy complex received support from rising soymeal futures, which have climbed on expectations that European Union demand could rise due to the bloc's new deforestation rules set to take effect in late December.

  • CBOT January soybeans rose 22-1/4 cents to $12.66-1/4 a bushel.

  • CBOT January soymeal (SMF27) ended $4.20 higher at $362.30 per short ton, a 5-1/2-week high.

  • CBOT January soyoil ended 0.92 cent higher at 59.29 cents per pound.

data.title: ECB's next rate move will probably meet market expectations, Vujcic tells paper
data.description:
The European Central Bank's next interest-rate decision will probably be in line with the market's expectations of a rate rise, ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic said in an interview with Austrian newspaper Kurier published on Friday.

"As things currently stand, I think market expectations will probably become true, as long as nothing unexpected happens in the meantime," the newspaper quoted Vujcic as saying in a joint interview with Austrian ECB policymaker Martin Kocher when asked about the next rate-setting meeting next month.

data.title: Oil Futures Settle Lower Ahead of OPEC+ Policy Meeting — Market Talk
data.description: Oil futures end the session lower with the market awaiting the weekend meeting of OPEC and its allies to discuss output policy for 2027. The gathering in Vienna will be "one of the most complicated OPEC+ meetings in years," Jorge Leon of Rystad Energy says in a note. The war in the Middle East has made current production a poor guide for what members can sustain, and "they are being asked to set quotas for a market whose 2027 balance depends entirely on how fast the Strait of Hormuz reopens to commercial traffic, which none of them controls." WTI settles down 0.7% at $83.08 a barrel for a 0.4% weekly loss. Brent falls 1.2% to $95.44, but snaps a three-week losing streak with a 3.1% weekly gain. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: CBOT wheat edges higher in light trading
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ticked higher on Friday amid light holiday trading and spillover support from rising soybean futures.

  • Traders continue to keep a close eye on the ongoing conflict in the Black Sea.

  • Ukraine has offered a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports and passed this on to international allies, Kyiv's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Friday.

  • Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Latvia on Friday of creating artificial obstacles to hinder the transit of Russian grain to global markets, saying the restrictions posed additional risks to global food security.

  • Russian Arctic seaport of Murmansk has signed a contract to ship 600,000 metric tons of grain for export by September 2027, the port's managing company said on Friday.

  • The company disclosed neither the supplier nor the buyer.

  • Trade volume has been relatively light between Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday and ahead of the weekend. Grain markets were closed for Thanksgiving and traded for an abbreviated session on Friday.

  • CBOT March wheat settled 3-1/2 cents higher to $5.91 per bushel.

  • K.C. March hard red winter wheat (KWH27) settled 5-1/2 cents higher to $6.36 per bushel.

  • Minneapolis March spring wheat (MWEH27) settled 7 cents higher to $6.53-1/2 per bushel.

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Front-month gold futures rose 2.9% in New York to $3,639.60 a troy ounce for a weekly gain of 3.5%. Silver rose 7.8% to $43.167 a troy ounce, its largest single-day percentage gain since Feb. 3, and was up 5.1% on the week. Platinum rose 6% to $1,313.90 a troy ounce. The gains offer some relief, but all three metals remain significantly lower year to date.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com and Adam Whittaker at adam.whittaker@wsj.com

data.title: Chief Operating Officer James C. Clancy to Lead Sales and Marketing Organizations
data.description:
Quantum Corporation () ("Quantum" or the "Company"), today announced that Chief Operating Officer James C. Clancy is assuming leadership of the Company’s sales and marketing organizations. The Company’s three regional sales vice presidents, as well as its vice president of marketing, will report directly to Clancy effective immediately.

“Jim is an industry veteran whose experience in sales leadership and execution speaks for itself,” commented Hugues Meyrath, President and Chief Executive Officer of Quantum. “With Jim’s proven track record in driving enterprise storage sales performance and go-to-market leadership, we believe that increasing his direct involvement in our sales and marketing practices will support our ongoing efforts to improve the Company’s operational efficiency and deliver value to customers, partners, and shareholders worldwide.”

Clancy is an accomplished technology executive with extensive expertise in global data protection, cyber recovery, enterprise storage, and go-to-market leadership. Throughout his career, Clancy has held leadership roles across some of the industry’s most recognized companies. Most notably, as President of Global Storage Sales at Dell, he drove significant global sales growth worldwide. As Senior Vice President of Global Sales for Dell EMC’s Data Protection Solutions, he enhanced sales and data efficiency for the industry leader. Clancy also served as Senior Vice President at Dell Technologies, where he provided strategic leadership to improve customer relationships, streamline operations, and drive profitable revenue growth. Earlier roles also include Divisional Vice President of Americas for EMC’s Backup Recovery Systems Division and Specialty Sales Management at EMC Corporation (now Dell EMC, DPS). Clancy has also served as a business advisor to HYCU, Black Kite, Index Engines, and Nexus Advisory Partners.

“Since joining Quantum, I have completed a deep-dive into the Company's operating model and growth opportunities,” said Clancy. "With that understanding, I am excited to take a more active role in leading the sales and marketing organizations and broadening the Company’s customer relationships. I believe this is a unique opportunity to build on the Company’s performance momentum and implement additional sales initiatives that will further our ability to accelerate growth and deliver end-to-end data management solutions designed for the AI era.”

The Company also announced the departure of Anthony Craythorne as the Company's Chief Revenue Officer. The Company does not have immediate plans to fill this position following his departure.

The Company also confirmed its previously issued guidance for its fiscal third quarter of 2027, as follows:

  • Revenue of $91.0 million, plus or minus $2 million
  • Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses of $28 million, plus or minus $1 million
  • Non-GAAP adjusted basic net income per share of $0.20, plus or minus $0.10
  • Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million, plus or minus $1 million

This assumes an effective annual tax rate of 3%; non-GAAP adjusted net income per share assumes an average basic share count of approximately 39.5 million in the fiscal third quarter of 2027. In addition, the Company cannot reconcile its non-GAAP guidance to the most directly comparable GAAP measures without unreasonable efforts because it cannot reliably predict warrant fair value changes, which depend on its future stock price, or the timing and amount of restructuring charges, special project costs and stock-based compensation expense. These items could materially affect GAAP results.

Quantum delivers end-to-end data management solutions designed for the AI era. With over four decades of experience, our data platform has allowed customers to extract the maximum value from their unique, unstructured data. From high-performance ingest that powers AI applications and demanding data-intensive workloads, to massive, durable data lakes to fuel AI models, Quantum delivers the most comprehensive and cost-efficient solutions. data.title: CBOT corn ticks higher on spillover support from soybeans

data.title: SA Asks: What's the best-positioned chip stock right now?
data.description:
In the wake of a sharp sell-off in AI-related names, what's the best-positioned chip stock right now for investors?

Seeking Alpha analysts Julian Lin and Mike Zaccardi weigh in with their picks.

Julian Lin: Nvidia may indeed fit the bill for one of the more contrarian picks among higher-quality names. But Micron might stand out despite the higher volatility. The company benefits regardless of whether NVDA cedes market share and looks poised to sustain tremendous profits for at least the next several years.

(Julian Lin leads the SA investing group Best of Breed Growth Stocks.)

Mike Zaccardi: While Nvidia's valuation remains compelling, I think Advanced Micro Devices offers a more favorable risk/reward play into year-end and early 2027. Shares took a hit last week, partly due to the broad chip selloff and partly due to a short report from Hunterbrook.

As I detailed last week, there are some technical levels to watch, along with its low valuation. Investors also should be on guard for possible regulatory risk next year as the new Congress takes control of Capitol Hill. While I don't expect dramatic shifts, policy headwinds could persist next year and beyond.

data.title: Oil Futures Settle Lower Ahead of OPEC+ Policy Meeting — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil futures settled lower Friday with traders weighing renewed threats to Middle Eastern supplies and awaiting a weekend meeting of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies to discuss output policy for 2027.

Brent crude for January delivery fell 1.2% to $95.44 a barrel, ending the week up 3.1% and snapping a three-week losing streak. West Texas Intermediate crude for January fell 0.7% to $83.08 a barrel and was down a 0.4% from a week earlier, a fourth consecutive weekly loss.

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said Thursday that an attack on the Jazan oil refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations. Authorities were assessing the damage and checking the safety of the facilities, the ministry said.

Meanwhile, an Iranian drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians, The Wall Street Journal reported. Iran denied responsibility for the attack, which comes as negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain deadlocked despite a ceasefire.

"Prices had been under pressure for roughly four weeks as the market leaned into surplus talk," Price Futures Group senior market analyst Phil Flynn said in a note. But attacks on Saudi infrastructure and continued incidents around the Strait of Hormuz have put risk premium back, he added.

Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain at just 31% of prewar levels, according to preliminary data from Kpler. While Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong, delays to some November and December cargoes have raised concerns over the reliability of near-term Middle Eastern supplies, Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider, said.

OPEC and other producers in the broader group called OPEC+ are expected to discuss their collective output policy for 2027 on Sunday, with existing production agreements set to expire at the end of this year.

The group's assessment of members' sustainable production capacities will help determine individual output quotas for next year. However, disruptions to production and exports during the Iran war have complicated efforts to establish how much individual countries can pump.

It remains unclear whether Saudi Arabia--the cartel's de-facto leader--and other members will restore more supply, maintain current restrictions or consider fresh cuts to support prices.

The impact on oil prices of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting is likely to be tempered by the outlook for the regional conflict, analysts at MUFG said in a note Friday.

The meeting could end without a final decision, leaving current production quotas in place for the time being, Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht said. With the exception of Iraq, most OPEC+ members are producing well below their existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to increase output further, she said.

"Long-running tensions within the group may surface over output quota decisions," and disputes among members could weaken the group's pricing power, Capital Economics senior climate and commodities economist Hamad Hussain said in a note. "A more fractious and less cohesive OPEC+ will lead to greater oil price volatility and skew the balance of risks towards lower oil prices over time."

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Lithium Price Outlook as Sellers Target 80,000 Yuan After Failed Recovery
data.description:
Excess supply has dragged down prices from 2026 peaks, while soft new offers drove futures towards 80,000 yuan a tonne.

According to market data, there is renewed hesitation among buyers after an attempted recovery from oversupply, even as a now-larger yawning gap between past peaks and current levels begs the question of where the market might find its next bottom.

LITHIUM FUTURES RETREAT AS SELLERS DEFEND 84,000 YUAN LEVEL

The X update illustrates lithium carbonate futures trying but failing to maintain an attempted bounce. The Jan LC2701 contract was at 82,100 yuan a tonne, down 2.47% for the session.

The analyst chart shows the contract opened at 84,000 yuan and hit 85,100 yuan during trading. Source: Carl Via X

Prices were driven by sellers down to 82,080 yuan, near the bottom of the session. Trading volume was 199,813 lots; open interest was 324,382 lots.

The bearish reversal from 85,100 yuan indicates momentum buyers are no longer driving the market higher. The 84,000-yuan opening mark may serve as initial resistance. If the market recovers above 85,100 yuan, that would be a better sign of fresh buying support.

For now, 82,080 yuan is support, and a firm close below it is likely to test the 80,000-yuan psychological level. Capolingua analysis also indicates the presence of excess supply and may still be on the rally to the seller.

TRADING ECONOMICS SHOWS A PROLONGED PRICE DECLINE

Trading Economics' chart over a year shows lithium carbonate tumbling from around 200,000 yuan per tonne in May to 86,100 yuan as of 26 November. That's a big correction since the top of the year.

The chart shows a series of failed recoveries in the second half of 2026. Source: Trading Economics

A failed rally towards 140,000 yuan in August was followed by a rally to 160,000 yuan in September. A renewed selling bout saw the market accelerate through October and November.

86,100 is the most recent reading, which is a year-over-year decrease of 7.72%. The previous region at 90,000 yuan offers a key rebound benchmark, and between 95,000 and 100,000 yuan are higher thresholds. A concerted break above these areas would signal a pickup in price momentum.

The psychological level of 80,000 yuan still acts as a key downside reference. However, the chart hasn't formed a confirmed reversal or a reliable price support.

The broader market backdrop also encourages restraint. Trading Economics cites abundant supply, higher inventories, and a softer demand outlook.

WHAT LITHIUM INVESTORS SHOULD WATCH NEXT

Investors should observe whether LC2701 is able to hold at 82,080 yuan or if it tests down to 80,000 yuan. On the upside, the resistance zone to recover to is 84,000–85,100 yuan. Keep an eye on spot-market deals, battery manufacturer procurement, and inventory trends.

China's lithium spodumene imports above one million tonnes in October prompted more worries about raw-material availability. Stable lithium prices can be underpinned by sustained tight supply or relatively resilient downstream procurement.

When it comes to supply, the relatively slower restarting of spodumene mines and solid low-end battery-sector demand may linger at this stage.

data.title: OpenAI Reportedly Fires Back At Apple Over Trade Secrets And Hardware Suppliers
data.description:
Key points:
  • OpenAI also claims a former OpenAI worker who returned to Apple disclosed information about OpenAI’s product plans.
  • The dispute deepens a rift between the two companies, which partnered to integrate ChatGPT into iPhones two years ago before OpenAI bought former Apple design chief Jony Ive’s studio, io, for $6.4 billion. 
  • The filing follows Apple’s summer allegations that former staffers, including OpenAI chief hardware officer Tang Tan, leaked confidential product and supply chain data.

OpenAI has countersued Apple with a California lawsuit accusing the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets and squeezing hardware suppliers to block rival devices, the FT reported on Friday.

The complaint escalates a bitter legal clash between two Silicon Valley powerhouses that teamed up two years ago to bring ChatGPT into the iPhone. The filing comes after OpenAI’s $6.4 billion acquisition in May 2025 of io, a design studio led by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, as the artificial intelligence company prepares personal devices aimed at challenging Apple on its home turf.

Supply Chain Pressure And Talent Claims

OpenAI alleges that Apple is leveraging its financial scale and market weight to choke off competition and intimidate vendors that could assist with OpenAI’s new hardware. While Apple has long used upfront payments to secure scarce manufacturing capacity and cutting-edge chips, OpenAI contends the company has gone further by threatening and coercing suppliers working with both firms.

The AI company also claims a former OpenAI worker who returned to Apple disclosed information about OpenAI’s product plans and vendor relationships.

Earlier Lawsuit

Friday’s filing mirrors and counters allegations Apple raised in July against several departing employees, including OpenAI chief hardware officer Tang Tan, whom Apple accused of sharing confidential product development and supply chain details. Apple also claimed a former engineer took advantage of a network storage vulnerability to take proprietary files after leaving.

OpenAI rejected those claims in August, calling Apple’s suit an effort to curb its hiring of Apple talent. In its latest court filing, OpenAI argued that Apple pushed staff to keep work files on personal devices and cloud accounts, likening employment in Cupertino to a trap where workers can check out yet never truly leave.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment on OpenAI was ‘neutral’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

data.title: Why is Credicorp stock rocketing higher today
data.description:
What happened?

Shares of Credicorp jumped 5.6% in the morning session after U.S. equities rose in a holiday-shortened session supported by a bounce in technology stocks, CNBC reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged higher by 1.18%, or 591.99 points, to 50,774.94, while the S&P 500 edged higher by 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.31% to 24,129.50, according to the report. The report also showed that Meta Platforms rose more than 3%, Amazon rose about 4%, Broadcom rose almost 4% and Anthropic soared nearly 11%.

The gains capped weekly advances in which the Dow and S&P 500 each soared more than 5% and the Nasdaq soared more than 6%, the report said. Meanwhile, the VIX volatility index, a gauge of how much the S&P 500 might move in the next 30 days based on options trading, pulled back to 25.13, according to the report.

Broad rallies in major equity indexes often reflect improved investor risk appetite across the stock market. Bank shares can rise alongside the wider market when stronger sentiment encourages investors to buy economically sensitive stocks.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down and closed the day at $360.44, up 2.7% from the previous close.

What is the market telling us

Credicorp’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 9 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 2 days ago when the stock gained 2.2% on the news that third-quarter 2026 U.S. economic growth accelerated, October 2026 personal income and consumer prices rose and weekly unemployment claims declined.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported in its second estimate that real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, up from 2.2% in the second quarter. The agency revised real GDP up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. In a separate release, the BEA reported that the October 2026 personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.8% from one year earlier and 0.3% from the previous month. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 3.3% year on year and 0.3% monthly, while personal income increased $201.8 billion, or 0.7%, and personal consumption expenditures rose $63.8 billion, or 0.3%.

Separately, the U.S. Department of Labor reported that seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims fell by 13,000 to 189,000 in the week ending November 21, 2026, from the previous week's revised level of 202,000. The 4-week moving average decreased by 1,500 to 196,000 from the previous week's revised average of 197,500. Stronger economic growth and lower unemployment claims can boost demand for loans and reduce credit losses for banks, while elevated inflation can keep interest rates higher for longer. Investors often weigh the benefits of healthy borrowing activity against the risk that higher rates can pressure loan demand and asset values.

Credicorp is up 33.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $381.25 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $402.27 from July 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Credicorp’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $3,218.

ALSO WORTH WATCHING: Nvidia’s Quiet Partner. Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Front-month gold futures rose 2.9% in New York to $3,639.60 a troy ounce for a weekly gain of 3.5%. Silver rose 7.8% to $43.167 a troy ounce, its largest single-day percentage gain since Feb. 3, and was up 5.1% on the week. Platinum rose 6% to $1,313.90 a troy ounce. The gains offer some relief, but all three metals remain significantly lower year to date.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

data.title: NevGold Announces Graduation to the TSX Senior Board
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NevGold Corp. (TSX-V: NAU) OTCQX:NAUFF Frankfurt:5E50 (“NevGold” or the “Company“) is pleased to announce that the Company will graduate from the TSX Venture Exchange to the senior board Toronto Stock Exchange (the “TSX”) and the common shares of the Company will commence trading on the TSX at the opening of the market on or about December 1, 2026 under its current symbol “NAU”.

CEO, Brandon Bonifacio states “Since forming NevGold and completing our public listing in 2021, we have transformed the Company from an early-stage explorer into a well-funded developer with a portfolio of highly prospective gold, antimony, and copper assets in the Western United States. Our graduation to the TSX from the TSX Venture Exchange is a significant achievement that reflects the hard work of our team and the substantial progress we have made in building shareholder value.

Listing on Canada’s premier senior exchange represents an important milestone in NevGold’s evolution and positions the Company for its next phase of growth. We expect the TSX listing to increase our visibility among institutional and retail investors globally, expand access to capital, and further enhance our standing within the investment community.

As we continue advancing our flagship projects, particularly at a time when domestic sources of critical minerals such as antimony are becoming increasingly strategic, we remain committed to executing our long-term growth strategy and progressing toward becoming a leading emerging gold and antimony producer in North America.”

The Company has received final approval from the TSX for the listing of its common shares. In connection with the listing, the common shares will be voluntarily delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange upon the commencement of trading on the main TSX board.

The Company’s trading symbol will remain “NAU” upon the commencement of trading on the main TSX board. The CUSIP and ISIN will also remain unchanged. Shareholders are not required to take any action in connection with the Company’s graduation to the TSX, and existing share certificates and direct registration statements will continue to represent Nevgold’s common shares.

In connection with the listing on the TSX, the Company has reconstituted its audit committee to consist of Victor Bradley, Sean Waller and Scott Bensing, each of which is independent as determined under National Instrument 52-110 – Audit Committees. Victor Bradley has been appointed as the lead independent director of the Company.

About the Company

NevGold is dedicated to discovering, de-risking, and rapidly advancing gold and critical metals projects across premier jurisdictions in Nevada and Idaho to drive shareholder value and strengthen US mineral security. The Company holds a 100% interest in the Limousine Butte (gold-antimony) and Cedar Wash (gold) projects in Nevada, and the Nutmeg Mountain (gold) and Zeus (copper) projects in Idaho. data.title: Amazon, Target and Walmart Chase Holiday Toy Spending
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN, Financials), Walmart and Target are competing for holiday shoppers as demand for sensory toys, gaming consoles and consumer electronics shapes Black Friday shopping trends.

Squishy collectible toys rank among the most popular items at Amazon and Target, while interactive products and artificial intelligence-powered toys are also attracting consumer interest.

The $130 Stickerbox uses artificial intelligence to generate custom sticker designs, while the Primal Hatch megalodon toy is available at Amazon, Walmart and Target, with Amazon offering it for $35.

Consumer electronics remain a significant category for holiday retailers. According to the Consumer Technology Association, at least 87% of adults plan to purchase technology gifts this holiday season.

Popular electronics include Apple's AirPods 5, Sony cameras and Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.

Nintendo's $500 Switch 2 console also ranks among bestselling products at Amazon, Target and Best Buy, reflecting continued demand for gaming hardware.

Meanwhile, Mattel is expanding its KPop Demon Hunters toy lineup, while Disney is offering figurines based on its Toy Story franchise.

Investors will monitor Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales for indications of consumer spending strength, retail demand and fourth-quarter revenue performance.
